epoch_boundary_aligned.meaning: the exact end timestamp of the previous epoch aligns with the start of the new epoch
epoch_boundary_aligned.checkpoint: before claimRewards() for the previous epoch
epoch_boundary_aligned.evidence: The protocol fails to enforcecontinuous time-weighted lock across the entire epoch. Because the exact end timestamp of the previous epoch perfectly aligns with the start of the new epoch, an attacker can execute a deposit transaction right before the epoch concludes.

The bug stems from how TrustBonding evaluates historical balances. When a user calls claimRewards(), the contract fetches their eligible rewards via `_userEligibleRewardsForEpoch()`, which in turn queries userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd().
- malicious user can wait until the epoch ends, deposit capital with zero time-risk, and extract a massive share of the rewards, directly diluting users who held liquidity risk for the entire epoch.
